"""Tests for corpus normalisation and the corpus_ingest nodes."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest

from cybernaut_mini.corpus import (
    CorpusNormalizeError,
    CorpusSourceConfig,
    derive_title,
    make_document_id,
    normalize_rows,
)
from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest.nodes import (
    normalize_corpus,
    select_documents,
    snapshot_raw_corpus,
)

# Mirrors the NOSIBLE Hugging Face schema: text / label / netloc / url.
_HF_CONFIG = CorpusSourceConfig(
    field_map={"text": "text", "url": "url"},
    metadata_fields=["label", "netloc"],
    default_language="en",
    id_prefix="pred",
    min_text_chars=32,
)


def _row(index: int, text: str | None = None, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    row = {
        "text": text
        if text is not None
        else f"Analysts expect conditions to improve materially during the coming quarter {index}.",
        "label": "prediction",
        "netloc": "example.com",
        "url": f"https://example.com/article-{index}",
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Title derivation                                                    #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_title_is_the_first_sentence() -> None:
    assert derive_title("First sentence here. Second one follows.") == "First sentence here."


def test_long_title_is_cut_on_a_word_boundary() -> None:
    text = " ".join(["word"] * 60) + "."
    title = derive_title(text)
    assert len(title) <= 120
    assert not title.endswith("wor")  # never mid-word


def test_single_overlong_token_is_still_truncated() -> None:
    title = derive_title("x" * 400)
    assert len(title) == 120


def test_title_falls_back_to_whole_text_without_punctuation() -> None:
    assert derive_title("no terminal punctuation here") == "no terminal punctuation here"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Id stability                                                        #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_document_id_is_stable_across_runs() -> None:
    first = make_document_id("pred", "https://example.com/a")
    second = make_document_id("pred", "https://example.com/a")
    assert first == second
    assert first.startswith("pred-")


def test_different_keys_yield_different_ids() -> None:
    assert make_document_id("pred", "a") != make_document_id("pred", "b")


def test_ids_are_independent_of_row_order() -> None:
    rows = [_row(i) for i in range(5)]
    forward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)]
    backward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(list(reversed(rows)), _HF_CONFIG)]
    assert forward == backward


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Normalisation                                                       #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_hf_schema_maps_onto_document() -> None:
    documents = normalize_rows([_row(1)], _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len(documents) == 1
    doc = documents[0]
    assert doc.url == "https://example.com/article-1"
    assert doc.language == "en"
    assert doc.metadata == {"label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com"}
    assert doc.title
    assert doc.text


def test_short_rows_are_skipped_not_raised() -> None:
    """A 100k-row public corpus contains junk; one bad row must not fail a build."""
    rows = [_row(1), _row(2, text="too short")]
    documents = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len(documents) == 1


def test_duplicate_urls_collapse() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1), _row(1)]
    assert len(normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)) == 1


def test_rows_without_url_still_get_stable_distinct_ids() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1, url=""), _row(2, url="")]
    documents = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len({d.id for d in documents}) == 2


def test_empty_source_returns_empty() -> None:
    assert normalize_rows([], _HF_CONFIG) == []


def test_missing_text_column_is_a_hard_error() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(CorpusNormalizeError, match="absent"):
        normalize_rows([{"body": "x" * 100}], _HF_CONFIG)


def test_field_map_without_text_target_is_rejected() -> None:
    config = CorpusSourceConfig(field_map={"url": "url"})
    with pytest.raises(CorpusNormalizeError, match="exactly one"):
        normalize_rows([{"url": "https://example.com"}], config)


def test_whitespace_is_collapsed() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1, text="Lots   of \n\n irregular \t whitespace in this passage body here.")]
    doc = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)[0]
    assert "  " not in doc.text
    assert "\n" not in doc.text


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Nodes                                                               #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_snapshot_refuses_an_empty_source() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero rows"):
        snapshot_raw_corpus([])


def test_snapshot_passes_rows_through_unchanged() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1)]
    assert snapshot_raw_corpus(rows) == rows


def test_normalize_node_reports_total_wipeout() -> None:
    """Every row filtered out is a config error, not an empty result."""
    params = _HF_CONFIG.model_dump()
    params["min_text_chars"] = 10_000
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero documents"):
        normalize_corpus([_row(1)], params)


def test_select_caps_deterministically() -> None:
    normalized = normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(10)], _HF_CONFIG)
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalized]
    first = select_documents(documents, {"max_documents": 4})
    second = select_documents(list(reversed(documents)), {"max_documents": 4})
    assert len(first) == 4
    assert [d["id"] for d in first] == [d["id"] for d in second]


def test_select_filters_by_language() -> None:
    normalized = normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(3)], _HF_CONFIG)
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalized]
    documents[0]["language"] = "de"
    kept = select_documents(documents, {"languages": ["en"]})
    assert len(kept) == 2


def test_select_filters_by_metadata() -> None:
    rows = [_row(0), _row(1, label="not-prediction")]
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)]
    kept = select_documents(documents, {"metadata_equals": {"label": "prediction"}})
    assert len(kept) == 1
    assert kept[0]["metadata"]["label"] == "prediction"


def test_select_rejects_an_empty_result() -> None:
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows([_row(1)], _HF_CONFIG)]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero documents"):
        select_documents(documents, {"languages": ["fr"]})


def test_normalized_documents_survive_a_real_index_build() -> None:
    """Normalised output must satisfy the same validation the build applies."""
    from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.index_build.nodes import ingest_documents

    documents = [
        d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(6)], _HF_CONFIG)
    ]
    assert len(ingest_documents(documents)) == 6

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL → Judgment loader                                            #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def _miracl_row(
    query_id: str,
    question: str,
    positives: list[str],
    negatives: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a minimal structured MIRACL row (as load_dataset would return)."""
    return {
        "query_id": query_id,
        "query": question,
        "positive_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in positives],
        "negative_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in (negatives or [])],
    }


def test_load_miracl_judgments_maps_query_id_and_question() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("42", "What is the speed of light?", ["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "42"
    assert judgments[0].question == "What is the speed of light?"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_prefixes_docids_with_mir() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_ids = set(judgments[0].relevant_document_ids.keys())
    expected_pos = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    expected_neg = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert expected_pos in doc_ids
    assert expected_neg in doc_ids
    # All ids start with the mir prefix
    assert all(k.startswith("mir-") for k in doc_ids)


def test_load_miracl_judgments_preserves_grades() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    pos_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    neg_id = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[pos_id] == 1
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[neg_id] == 0


def test_load_miracl_judgments_skips_rows_with_no_assessments() -> None:
    rows = [
        _miracl_row("1", "has passages", positives=["12#0"]),
        _miracl_row("2", "no passages", positives=[], negatives=[]),
    ]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "1"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_raises_on_empty_input() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero rows"):
        load_miracl_judgments([])


def test_load_miracl_judgments_returns_valid_judgment_models() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("7", "Q?", positives=["5#0", "5#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert all(isinstance(j, Judgment) for j in judgments)


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_passes_when_all_present() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    # No exception should be raised when the corpus contains the id.
    validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids={doc_id})


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_raises_on_missing_docid() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="absent from corpus"):
        validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids=set())


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_lists_missing_ids_in_error() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0", "13#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mir-"):
        validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids=set())


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Kedro node wrappers                                                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_build_miracl_judgments_node_returns_serialisable_dicts() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    result = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert isinstance(result[0], dict)
    assert result[0]["query_id"] == "1"
    assert isinstance(result[0]["relevant_document_ids"], dict)


def test_validate_judgments_node_passes_through_when_corpus_matches() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgment_dicts = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    documents = [{"id": doc_id, "title": "T", "text": "Body text here.", "language": "en"}]
    result = validate_judgments(judgment_dicts, documents)
    # Node is a pass-through on success
    assert result == judgment_dicts


def test_validate_judgments_node_raises_on_missing_doc() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["missing#0"])]
    judgment_dicts = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="absent from corpus"):
        validate_judgments(judgment_dicts, documents=[])

def _miracl_row(
    query_id: str,
    question: str,
    positives: list[str],
    negatives: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a minimal structured MIRACL row (as load_dataset would return)."""
    return {
        "query_id": query_id,
        "query": question,
        "positive_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in positives],
        "negative_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in (negatives or [])],
    }


def test_load_miracl_judgments_maps_query_id_and_question() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("42", "What is the speed of light?", ["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "42"
    assert judgments[0].question == "What is the speed of light?"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_prefixes_docids_with_mir() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_ids = set(judgments[0].relevant_document_ids.keys())
    expected_pos = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    expected_neg = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert expected_pos in doc_ids
    assert expected_neg in doc_ids
    # All ids start with the mir prefix
    assert all(k.startswith("mir-") for k in doc_ids)


def test_load_miracl_judgments_preserves_grades() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    pos_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    neg_id = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[pos_id] == 1
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[neg_id] == 0


def test_load_miracl_judgments_skips_rows_with_no_assessments() -> None:
    rows = [
        _miracl_row("1", "has passages", positives=["12#0"]),
        _miracl_row("2", "no passages", positives=[], negatives=[]),
    ]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "1"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_raises_on_empty_input() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero rows"):
        load_miracl_judgments([])


def test_load_miracl_judgments_returns_valid_judgment_models() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("7", "Q?", positives=["5#0", "5#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert all(isinstance(j, Judgment) for j in judgments)


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_passes_when_all_present() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    # No exception should be raised when the corpus contains the id.
    validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids={doc_id})


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_raises_on_missing_docid() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="absent from corpus"):
        validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids=set())


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_lists_missing_ids_in_error() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0", "13#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mir-"):
        validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids=set())


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Kedro node wrappers                                                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_build_miracl_judgments_node_returns_serialisable_dicts() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    result = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert isinstance(result[0], dict)
    assert result[0]["query_id"] == "1"
    assert isinstance(result[0]["relevant_document_ids"], dict)


def test_validate_judgments_node_passes_through_when_corpus_matches() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgment_dicts = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    documents = [{"id": doc_id, "title": "T", "text": "Body text here.", "language": "en"}]
    result = validate_judgments(judgment_dicts, documents)
    # Node is a pass-through on success
    assert result == judgment_dicts


def test_validate_judgments_node_raises_on_missing_doc() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["missing#0"])]
    judgment_dicts = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="absent from corpus"):
        validate_judgments(judgment_dicts, documents=[])

"""Tests for corpus normalisation and the corpus_ingest nodes."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest

from cybernaut_mini.corpus import (
    CorpusNormalizeError,
    CorpusSourceConfig,
    derive_title,
    load_miracl_judgments,
    make_document_id,
    normalize_rows,
    validate_judgments_against_corpus,
)
from cybernaut_mini.models import Judgment
from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest.nodes import (
    build_miracl_judgments,
    normalize_corpus,
    select_documents,
    snapshot_raw_corpus,
    validate_judgments,
)

# Mirrors the NOSIBLE Hugging Face schema: text / label / netloc / url.
_HF_CONFIG = CorpusSourceConfig(
    field_map={"text": "text", "url": "url"},
    metadata_fields=["label", "netloc"],
    default_language="en",
    id_prefix="pred",
    min_text_chars=32,
)


def _row(index: int, text: str | None = None, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    row = {
        "text": text
        if text is not None
        else f"Analysts expect conditions to improve materially during the coming quarter {index}.",
        "label": "prediction",
        "netloc": "example.com",
        "url": f"https://example.com/article-{index}",
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Title derivation                                                    #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_title_is_the_first_sentence() -> None:
    assert derive_title("First sentence here. Second one follows.") == "First sentence here."


def test_long_title_is_cut_on_a_word_boundary() -> None:
    text = " ".join(["word"] * 60) + "."
    title = derive_title(text)
    assert len(title) <= 120
    assert not title.endswith("wor")  # never mid-word


def test_single_overlong_token_is_still_truncated() -> None:
    title = derive_title("x" * 400)
    assert len(title) == 120


def test_title_falls_back_to_whole_text_without_punctuation() -> None:
    assert derive_title("no terminal punctuation here") == "no terminal punctuation here"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Id stability                                                        #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_document_id_is_stable_across_runs() -> None:
    first = make_document_id("pred", "https://example.com/a")
    second = make_document_id("pred", "https://example.com/a")
    assert first == second
    assert first.startswith("pred-")


def test_different_keys_yield_different_ids() -> None:
    assert make_document_id("pred", "a") != make_document_id("pred", "b")


def test_ids_are_independent_of_row_order() -> None:
    rows = [_row(i) for i in range(5)]
    forward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)]
    backward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(list(reversed(rows)), _HF_CONFIG)]
    assert forward == backward


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Normalisation                                                       #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_hf_schema_maps_onto_document() -> None:
    documents = normalize_rows([_row(1)], _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len(documents) == 1
    doc = documents[0]
    assert doc.url == "https://example.com/article-1"
    assert doc.language == "en"
    assert doc.metadata == {"label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com"}
    assert doc.title
    assert doc.text


def test_short_rows_are_skipped_not_raised() -> None:
    """A 100k-row public corpus contains junk; one bad row must not fail a build."""
    rows = [_row(1), _row(2, text="too short")]
    documents = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len(documents) == 1


def test_duplicate_urls_collapse() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1), _row(1)]
    assert len(normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)) == 1


def test_rows_without_url_still_get_stable_distinct_ids() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1, url=""), _row(2, url="")]
    documents = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len({d.id for d in documents}) == 2


def test_empty_source_returns_empty() -> None:
    assert normalize_rows([], _HF_CONFIG) == []


def test_missing_text_column_is_a_hard_error() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(CorpusNormalizeError, match="absent"):
        normalize_rows([{"body": "x" * 100}], _HF_CONFIG)


def test_field_map_without_text_target_is_rejected() -> None:
    config = CorpusSourceConfig(field_map={"url": "url"})
    with pytest.raises(CorpusNormalizeError, match="exactly one"):
        normalize_rows([{"url": "https://example.com"}], config)


def test_whitespace_is_collapsed() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1, text="Lots   of \n\n irregular \t whitespace in this passage body here.")]
    doc = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)[0]
    assert "  " not in doc.text
    assert "\n" not in doc.text


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Nodes                                                               #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_snapshot_refuses_an_empty_source() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero rows"):
        snapshot_raw_corpus([])


def test_snapshot_passes_rows_through_unchanged() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1)]
    assert snapshot_raw_corpus(rows) == rows


def test_normalize_node_reports_total_wipeout() -> None:
    """Every row filtered out is a config error, not an empty result."""
    params = _HF_CONFIG.model_dump()
    params["min_text_chars"] = 10_000
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero documents"):
        normalize_corpus([_row(1)], params)


def test_select_caps_deterministically() -> None:
    normalized = normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(10)], _HF_CONFIG)
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalized]
    first = select_documents(documents, {"max_documents": 4})
    second = select_documents(list(reversed(documents)), {"max_documents": 4})
    assert len(first) == 4
    assert [d["id"] for d in first] == [d["id"] for d in second]


def test_select_filters_by_language() -> None:
    normalized = normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(3)], _HF_CONFIG)
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalized]
    documents[0]["language"] = "de"
    kept = select_documents(documents, {"languages": ["en"]})
    assert len(kept) == 2


def test_select_filters_by_metadata() -> None:
    rows = [_row(0), _row(1, label="not-prediction")]
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)]
    kept = select_documents(documents, {"metadata_equals": {"label": "prediction"}})
    assert len(kept) == 1
    assert kept[0]["metadata"]["label"] == "prediction"


def test_select_rejects_an_empty_result() -> None:
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows([_row(1)], _HF_CONFIG)]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero documents"):
        select_documents(documents, {"languages": ["fr"]})


def test_normalized_documents_survive_a_real_index_build() -> None:
    """Normalised output must satisfy the same validation the build applies."""
    from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.index_build.nodes import ingest_documents

    documents = [
        d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(6)], _HF_CONFIG)
    ]
    assert len(ingest_documents(documents)) == 6

"""Tests for corpus normalisation and the corpus_ingest nodes."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest

from cybernaut_mini.corpus import (
    CorpusNormalizeError,
    CorpusSourceConfig,
    derive_title,
    load_miracl_judgments,
    make_document_id,
    normalize_rows,
    validate_judgments_against_corpus,
)
from cybernaut_mini.models import Judgment
from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest.nodes import (
    build_miracl_judgments,
    normalize_corpus,
    select_documents,
    snapshot_raw_corpus,
    validate_judgments,
)

# Mirrors the NOSIBLE Hugging Face schema: text / label / netloc / url.
_HF_CONFIG = CorpusSourceConfig(
    field_map={"text": "text", "url": "url"},
    metadata_fields=["label", "netloc"],
    default_language="en",
    id_prefix="pred",
    min_text_chars=32,
)


def _row(index: int, text: str | None = None, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    row = {
        "text": text
        if text is not None
        else f"Analysts expect conditions to improve materially during the coming quarter {index}.",
        "label": "prediction",
        "netloc": "example.com",
        "url": f"https://example.com/article-{index}",
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Title derivation                                                    #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_title_is_the_first_sentence() -> None:
    assert derive_title("First sentence here. Second one follows.") == "First sentence here."


def test_long_title_is_cut_on_a_word_boundary() -> None:
    text = " ".join(["word"] * 60) + "."
    title = derive_title(text)
    assert len(title) <= 120
    assert not title.endswith("wor")  # never mid-word


def test_single_overlong_token_is_still_truncated() -> None:
    title = derive_title("x" * 400)
    assert len(title) == 120


def test_title_falls_back_to_whole_text_without_punctuation() -> None:
    assert derive_title("no terminal punctuation here") == "no terminal punctuation here"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Id stability                                                        #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_document_id_is_stable_across_runs() -> None:
    first = make_document_id("pred", "https://example.com/a")
    second = make_document_id("pred", "https://example.com/a")
    assert first == second
    assert first.startswith("pred-")


def test_different_keys_yield_different_ids() -> None:
    assert make_document_id("pred", "a") != make_document_id("pred", "b")


def test_ids_are_independent_of_row_order() -> None:
    rows = [_row(i) for i in range(5)]
    forward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)]
    backward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(list(reversed(rows)), _HF_CONFIG)]
    assert forward == backward


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Normalisation                                                       #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_hf_schema_maps_onto_document() -> None:
    documents = normalize_rows([_row(1)], _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len(documents) == 1
    doc = documents[0]
    assert doc.url == "https://example.com/article-1"
    assert doc.language == "en"
    assert doc.metadata == {"label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com"}
    assert doc.title
    assert doc.text


def test_short_rows_are_skipped_not_raised() -> None:
    """A 100k-row public corpus contains junk; one bad row must not fail a build."""
    rows = [_row(1), _row(2, text="too short")]
    documents = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len(documents) == 1


def test_duplicate_urls_collapse() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1), _row(1)]
    assert len(normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)) == 1


def test_rows_without_url_still_get_stable_distinct_ids() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1, url=""), _row(2, url="")]
    documents = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)
    assert len({d.id for d in documents}) == 2


def test_empty_source_returns_empty() -> None:
    assert normalize_rows([], _HF_CONFIG) == []


def test_missing_text_column_is_a_hard_error() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(CorpusNormalizeError, match="absent"):
        normalize_rows([{"body": "x" * 100}], _HF_CONFIG)


def test_field_map_without_text_target_is_rejected() -> None:
    config = CorpusSourceConfig(field_map={"url": "url"})
    with pytest.raises(CorpusNormalizeError, match="exactly one"):
        normalize_rows([{"url": "https://example.com"}], config)


def test_whitespace_is_collapsed() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1, text="Lots   of \n\n irregular \t whitespace in this passage body here.")]
    doc = normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)[0]
    assert "  " not in doc.text
    assert "\n" not in doc.text

# Nodes                                                               #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def test_snapshot_refuses_an_empty_source() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero rows"):
        snapshot_raw_corpus([])


def test_snapshot_passes_rows_through_unchanged() -> None:
    rows = [_row(1)]
    assert snapshot_raw_corpus(rows) == rows


def test_normalize_node_reports_total_wipeout() -> None:
    """Every row filtered out is a config error, not an empty result."""
    params = _HF_CONFIG.model_dump()
    params["min_text_chars"] = 10_000
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero documents"):
        normalize_corpus([_row(1)], params)


def test_select_caps_deterministically() -> None:
    normalized = normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(10)], _HF_CONFIG)
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalized]
    first = select_documents(documents, {"max_documents": 4})
    second = select_documents(list(reversed(documents)), {"max_documents": 4})
    assert len(first) == 4
    assert [d["id"] for d in first] == [d["id"] for d in second]


def test_select_filters_by_language() -> None:
    normalized = normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(3)], _HF_CONFIG)
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalized]
    documents[0]["language"] = "de"
    kept = select_documents(documents, {"languages": ["en"]})
    assert len(kept) == 2


def test_select_filters_by_metadata() -> None:
    rows = [_row(0), _row(1, label="not-prediction")]
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows(rows, _HF_CONFIG)]
    kept = select_documents(documents, {"metadata_equals": {"label": "prediction"}})
    assert len(kept) == 1
    assert kept[0]["metadata"]["label"] == "prediction"


def test_select_rejects_an_empty_result() -> None:
    documents = [d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows([_row(1)], _HF_CONFIG)]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero documents"):
        select_documents(documents, {"languages": ["fr"]})


def test_normalized_documents_survive_a_real_index_build() -> None:
    """Normalised output must satisfy the same validation the build applies."""
    from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.index_build.nodes import ingest_documents

    documents = [
        d.model_dump(mode="json") for d in normalize_rows([_row(i) for i in range(6)], _HF_CONFIG)
    ]
    assert len(ingest_documents(documents)) == 6


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL → Judgment loader                                            #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #


def _miracl_row(
    query_id: str,
    question: str,
    positives: list[str],
    negatives: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a minimal structured MIRACL row (as load_dataset would return)."""
    return {
        "query_id": query_id,
        "query": question,
        "positive_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in positives],
        "negative_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in (negatives or [])],
    }


def test_load_miracl_judgments_maps_query_id_and_question() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("42", "What is the speed of light?", ["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "42"
    assert judgments[0].question == "What is the speed of light?"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_prefixes_docids_with_mir() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_ids = set(judgments[0].relevant_document_ids.keys())
    expected_pos = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    expected_neg = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert expected_pos in doc_ids
    assert expected_neg in doc_ids
    # All ids start with the mir prefix
    assert all(k.startswith("mir-") for k in doc_ids)


def test_load_miracl_judgments_preserves_grades() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    pos_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    neg_id = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[pos_id] == 1
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[neg_id] == 0


def test_load_miracl_judgments_skips_rows_with_no_assessments() -> None:
    rows = [
        _miracl_row("1", "has passages", positives=["12#0"]),
        _miracl_row("2", "no passages", positives=[], negatives=[]),
    ]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "1"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_raises_on_empty_input() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="zero rows"):
        load_miracl_judgments([])


def test_load_miracl_judgments_returns_valid_judgment_models() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("7", "Q?", positives=["5#0", "5#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert all(isinstance(j, Judgment) for j in judgments)


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_passes_when_all_present() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    # No exception should be raised when the corpus contains the id.
    validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids={doc_id})


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_raises_on_missing_docid() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="absent from corpus"):
        validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids=set())


def test_validate_judgments_against_corpus_lists_missing_ids_in_error() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0", "13#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mir-"):
        validate_judgments_against_corpus(judgments, corpus_doc_ids=set())

def test_build_miracl_judgments_node_returns_serialisable_dicts() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    result = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert isinstance(result[0], dict)
    assert result[0]["query_id"] == "1"
    assert isinstance(result[0]["relevant_document_ids"], dict)


def test_validate_judgments_node_passes_through_when_corpus_matches() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"])]
    judgment_dicts = build_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")

    result = validate_judgments(judgment_dicts, documents)

def test_validate_judgments_node_raises_on_missing_doc() -> None:

# Production catalog overrides: `kedro run --env prod --pipeline production`.
#
# Only the acquisition source changes. Every downstream entry is inherited from
# conf/base/catalog.yml unchanged, which is the point of routing data through the
# catalog: the pipeline code that builds a 100k-document shard is the same code
# that builds the 66-document sample.
#
# Requires the `hf` extra:  uv sync --extra hf --extra st
# Private/gated repos additionally need HF_TOKEN in the environment.

raw_corpus_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.HuggingFaceDataset
  repo_id: NOSIBLE/prediction
  # REQUIRED: an immutable commit SHA or tag. Branch names and this placeholder
  # are both rejected at load time, so an unpinned corpus cannot reach a build.
  # Resolved 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('NOSIBLE/prediction').sha)"
  revision: eefc2260041afc60bb8f8e343cf43a20e7828a4a
  split: train
  columns: [text, label, netloc, url]
  # Uncapped: the full 100,000 rows (26.9 MB parquet, 71.4 MB in Arrow). Set
  # max_rows to dial in a faster build; the cap is a prefix, not a sample, so a
  # capped run is not a statistically valid preview of the full one.

# Keep production artifacts out of the sample paths so a prod run can never
# overwrite the committed sample index.
raw_corpus:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/01_raw/prediction_snapshot.jsonl

normalized_documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/prediction_documents.jsonl

documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:input_path,data/03_primary/prediction_corpus.jsonl}

shard_index:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.ShardIndexDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:index_path,artifacts/prediction}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL en-dev judgment pipeline (task #5 / M1.4)                   #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Run standalone: kedro run --env prod --pipeline judgment_ingest
# Or as part of production (documents must exist first for validation).

miracl_en_dev_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.HuggingFaceDataset
  repo_id: miracl/miracl
  # SHA pinned 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('miracl/miracl').sha)"
  revision: 5be20db9509754dadad47689368639fcec739c00
  config: en
  split: dev
  streaming: true
  # Returns query_id, query, positive_passages (grade=1), negative_passages (grade=0).

miracl_judgments_unvalidated:

judgments:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl

"""Kedro pipeline registry: build and evaluation DAGs.

The search/agent side is request-time and dynamically branching, so it is a plain
library behind the Typer CLI, not a pipeline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from kedro.pipeline import Pipeline

from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest import create_pipeline as create_corpus_ingest
from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest.pipeline import create_judgment_pipeline
from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.evaluation import create_pipeline as create_evaluation
from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.index_build import create_pipeline as create_index_build


def register_pipelines() -> dict[str, Pipeline]:
    corpus_ingest = create_corpus_ingest()
    judgment_ingest = create_judgment_pipeline()
    index_build = create_index_build()
    evaluation = create_evaluation()
    pipelines: dict[str, Pipeline] = {
        "corpus_ingest": corpus_ingest,
        "judgment_ingest": judgment_ingest,
        "index_build": index_build,
        "evaluation": evaluation,
        # Acquisition then build: `kedro run --pipeline production` takes a pinned
        # source all the way to a queryable index, including validated judgments.
        "production": corpus_ingest + judgment_ingest + index_build,
        "__default__": index_build,
    }
    return pipelines

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## huggingface
You have tools for using the Hugging Face Hub. Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'neelan'
hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment. arXiv paper id's are often used as references between datasets, models and papers. ## numerai
IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS FOR USING THE NUMERAI MCP SERVER:

This server provides several tools for interacting with the Numerai Tournament API.
All functionality is accessed by calling these tools directly — they are already
available in your tool catalog via tools/list. Do NOT call list_mcp_resources or
list_mcp_resource_templates to discover functionality. The tools are already loaded.

When a user asks what you can do with Numerai, or asks about Numerai capabilities,
IMMEDIATELY all tools/list to list these tools and offer to call them. Do not search
for resources first.

TERMINOLOGY:
- "Models" are prediction algorithms submitted by participants
- "Accounts" are people/entities who own models — one account can have many models
- Tournament 8 = "Classic", 11 = "Signals", 12 = "CryptoSignals"

KEY METRICS:
- mmcRep = meta-model contribution reputation (main performance score)
- fncV3Rep = feature-neutral correlation v3 reputation
- return13Weeks = 13-week return on staked NMR
- nmrStaked = NMR cryptocurrency staked on the model
- latestReps = nested object with current reputation scores (corr, mmc, fnc)
- latestRanks = nested object with current rankings
- latestReturns = nested object with return data (oneDay, threeMonths, oneYear)

AUTH: Users pass API tokens via the Authorization header or the apiToken parameter.

2	
3	All JSON-bearing datasets serialize through :func:`cybernaut_mini.models.canonical_dumps`
4	so pipeline outputs keep the byte-for-byte determinism guarantee.

6	Every path the corpus and the index travel goes through a dataset in this module,
7	so the catalog — not a node body — owns all file and network I/O. That is what makes
8	``kedro-viz`` show real lineage and what lets ``conf/prod`` swap a local corpus for a
9	Hugging Face one without touching pipeline code.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import os
15	from pathlib import Path
16	from typing import Any
17	
18	import numpy as np
19	import numpy.typing as npt
20	from kedro.io import AbstractDataset
21	from kedro.io.core import DatasetError
22	
23	from cybernaut_mini.models import canonical_dumps
24	
25	#: Committed fixture directories. A pipeline writing here would silently rewrite the
26	#: golden corpus that the determinism tests compare against, so saves are refused.
27	#: Reads are unaffected — `--input data/sample/documents.jsonl` stays supported.
28	PROTECTED_DIRS = ("data/sample", "data/00_reference")
29	
30	
31	def _guard_protected(filepath: Path) -> None:
32	    """Refuse to write over a committed fixture."""
33	    try:
34	        relative = filepath.resolve().relative_to(Path.cwd().resolve())
35	    except ValueError:
36	        # Outside the project (e.g. a pytest tmp_path); nothing to protect.
37	        return
38	    as_posix = relative.as_posix()
39	    for protected in PROTECTED_DIRS:
40	        if as_posix == protected or as_posix.startswith(f"{protected}/"):
41	            msg = (
42	                f"refusing to write {as_posix}: {protected} holds committed fixtures. "
43	                f"Point this catalog entry at a generated layer "
44	                f"(data/01_raw, data/02_intermediate, data/03_primary) instead."
45	            )
46	            raise DatasetError(msg)

49	class CanonicalJsonDataset(AbstractDataset[Any, Any]):
50	    """A single JSON value written with the canonical writer."""
51	
52	    def __init__(self, filepath: str) -> None:
53	        self._filepath = Path(filepath)
54	
55	    def load(self) -> Any:
56	        import json
57	
58	        return json.loads(self._filepath.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
59	
60	    def save(self, data: Any) -> None:
61	        _guard_protected(self._filepath)
62	        self._filepath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
63	        self._filepath.write_text(canonical_dumps(data) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
64	
65	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
66	        return self._filepath.exists()

69	        return {"filepath": str(self._filepath)}

72	class JsonlDataset(AbstractDataset[list[Any], list[Any]]):
73	    """A list of JSON records, one canonical-JSON object per line."""
74	
75	    def __init__(self, filepath: str) -> None:
76	        self._filepath = Path(filepath)
77	
78	    def load(self) -> list[Any]:
79	        import json
80	
81	        if not self._filepath.exists():
82	            # A bare traceback here is unhelpful: the usual cause is running a build
83	            # before the pipeline that produces its input has ever run.
84	            msg = (
85	                f"{self._filepath} does not exist.\n"
86	                f"  If it is a pipeline output, produce it first: "
87	                f"`kedro run --pipeline corpus_ingest` (see conf/base/catalog.yml).\n"
88	                f"  If you meant an existing corpus, point at it: "
89	                f"`--params input_path=data/sample/documents.jsonl` "
90	                f"(CLI: `--input data/sample/documents.jsonl`)."
91	            )
92	            raise DatasetError(msg)
93	
94	        records: list[Any] = []
95	        with self._filepath.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
96	            for line in handle:
97	                line = line.strip()
98	                if line:
99	                    records.append(json.loads(line))
100	        return records
101	
102	    def save(self, data: list[Any]) -> None:
103	        _guard_protected(self._filepath)
104	        self._filepath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
105	        lines = "".join(canonical_dumps(record) + "\n" for record in data)
106	        self._filepath.write_text(lines, encoding="utf-8")
107	
108	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
109	        return self._filepath.exists()
110	
111	    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
112	        return {"filepath": str(self._filepath)}

137	class HuggingFaceDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
138	    """Read-only corpus source backed by a Hugging Face Hub dataset repo.
139	
140	    ``revision`` is **required and must be a commit SHA or tag**, never a branch
141	    name: a production shard is only reproducible if the corpus it was built from
142	    is pinned. ``main`` is rejected outright.
143	
144	    Set ``streaming=True`` for large datasets (CC-News is hundreds of GB in full):
145	    the loader opens an :class:`~datasets.IterableDataset` over Arrow shards and
146	    uses :func:`itertools.islice` so only ``max_rows`` rows are downloaded rather
147	    than materialising a whole shard boundary.
148	
149	    ``filter_equals`` pre-filters rows in streaming mode **before** the
150	    ``max_rows`` cap is applied, so the cap counts only rows that pass the
151	    filter. Use this to restrict a multilingual corpus to a single language
152	    without downloading rows that will be dropped — e.g. for CC-News:
153	    ``filter_equals: {language: en}``.
154	
155	    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — CC-News as a
156	        corpus source; 200k-document builds are the target scale (Phase 1.2).
157	
158	    Assumptions:
159	        - ``IterableDataset.features`` is populated from the dataset's Arrow
160	          schema metadata without iterating rows, so the missing-column check
161	          can inspect it before consuming any data. When ``features`` is
162	          ``None`` (a dynamically typed transform was chained upstream), the
163	          check falls back to the first row's keys and re-inserts that row so
164	          nothing is lost.
165	        - ``filter_equals`` is applied in streaming mode only. The eager path
166	          materialises the whole split first; for large multilingual corpora
167	          ``streaming=True`` is therefore mandatory.
168	
169	    Alternatives rejected:
170	        - ``IterableDataset.select_columns`` for projection in streaming mode.
171	          Supported since ``datasets>=2.4`` but adds another lazy wrapper; a
172	          per-row dict comprehension is simpler and independent of the exact
173	          ``datasets`` API version.
174	        - Filtering in ``select_documents`` rather than here: would download
175	          millions of non-English CC-News rows into the raw snapshot, wasting
176	          disk and network just to drop them.
177	
178	    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``). The import is deferred to
179	    :meth:`load` so the core package — and the whole offline test suite — never
180	    depends on it.
181	    """
182	
183	    #: Refs that move over time and so cannot pin a reproducible build.
184	    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
185	
186	    #: Shipped in conf/prod as a deliberate tripwire — a real SHA must replace it.
187	    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"
188	
189	    def __init__(
190	        self,
191	        repo_id: str,
192	        revision: str,
193	        split: str = "train",
194	        config: str | None = None,
195	        columns: list[str] | None = None,
196	        max_rows: int | None = None,
197	        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
198	        streaming: bool = False,
199	        filter_equals: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
200	    ) -> None:
201	        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
202	        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
203	            msg = (
204	                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
205	                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
206	                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
207	                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
208	            )
209	            raise DatasetError(msg)
210	        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
211	            msg = (
212	                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
213	                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}. A moving ref makes the built "
214	                f"index unreproducible."
215	            )
216	            raise DatasetError(msg)
217	        self._repo_id = repo_id
218	        self._revision = revision
219	        self._split = split
220	        self._config = config
221	        self._columns = columns
222	        self._max_rows = max_rows
223	        self._token_env = token_env
224	        self._streaming = streaming
225	        self._filter_equals = filter_equals
226	
227	    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
228	        try:
229	            # The Hugging Face `datasets` package, not this module: Python 3 has no
230	            # implicit relative imports, so the absolute name wins despite the clash.
231	            from datasets import load_dataset
232	        except ImportError as exc:
233	            msg = (
234	                "HuggingFaceDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
235	                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
236	            )
237	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
238	
239	        # A private repo needs a token; a public one must still work without it.
240	        token = os.environ.get(self._token_env) or None
241	
242	        if self._streaming:
243	            return self._load_streaming(load_dataset, token)
244	        return self._load_eager(load_dataset, token)
245	
246	    def _load_eager(self, load_dataset: Any, token: str | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
247	        """Non-streaming path: byte-identical to the original implementation."""
248	        split = self._split
249	        if self._max_rows is not None:
250	            # Slice in the split spec so only the requested rows are materialised.
251	            split = f"{split}[:{self._max_rows}]"
252	
253	        dataset = load_dataset(
254	            self._repo_id,
255	            self._config,
256	            revision=self._revision,
257	            split=split,
258	            token=token,
259	        )
260	        if self._columns is not None:
261	            missing = set(self._columns) - set(dataset.column_names)
262	            if missing:
263	                msg = (
264	                    f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}): requested columns "
265	                    f"{sorted(missing)} are absent; available: {sorted(dataset.column_names)}"
266	                )
267	                raise DatasetError(msg)
268	            dataset = dataset.select_columns(self._columns)
269	
270	        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = [dict(row) for row in dataset]
271	        return rows
272	
273	    def _load_streaming(self, load_dataset: Any, token: str | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
274	        """Streaming path: opens an IterableDataset and slices with islice."""
275	        import itertools
276	
277	        dataset = load_dataset(
278	            self._repo_id,
279	            self._config,
280	            revision=self._revision,
281	            split=self._split,
282	            token=token,
283	            streaming=True,
284	        )
285	
286	        it: Any = iter(dataset)
287	
288	        if self._columns is not None:
289	            # Prefer features (populated from Arrow schema, no rows consumed).
290	            features = getattr(dataset, "features", None)
291	            if features is not None:
292	                available = set(features.keys())
293	            else:
294	                # Fall back to the first row's keys; re-insert it so nothing is lost.
295	                try:
296	                    first_row = next(it)
297	                except StopIteration:
298	                    return []
299	                available = set(first_row.keys())
300	                it = itertools.chain([first_row], it)
301	
302	            missing = set(self._columns) - available
303	            if missing:
304	                msg = (
305	                    f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}): requested columns "
306	                    f"{sorted(missing)} are absent; available: {sorted(available)}"
307	                )
308	                raise DatasetError(msg)
309	
310	        # Apply filter_equals BEFORE max_rows so the cap counts only matching rows.
311	        if self._filter_equals is not None:
312	            fe = self._filter_equals
313	            it = (row for row in it if all(row.get(k) == v for k, v in fe.items()))
314	
315	        if self._max_rows is not None:
316	            it = itertools.islice(it, self._max_rows)
317	
318	        if self._columns is not None:
319	            cols = self._columns
320	            return [{col: row[col] for col in cols} for row in it]
321	        return [dict(row) for row in it]
322	
323	    def save(self, data: None) -> None:
324	        msg = (
325	            f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}) is read-only; write the "
326	            f"normalised corpus to a JsonlDataset in data/01_raw instead."
327	        )
328	        raise DatasetError(msg)
329	
330	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
331	        # Existence would require a network round-trip; report False so Kedro
332	        # never treats a Hub lookup as a cheap local check.
333	        return False
334	
335	    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
336	        return {
337	            "repo_id": self._repo_id,
338	            "revision": self._revision,
339	            "split": self._split,
340	            "config": self._config,
341	            "columns": self._columns,
342	            "max_rows": self._max_rows,
343	            "streaming": self._streaming,
344	            "filter_equals": self._filter_equals,
345	        }
346

348	class HfFileDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
349	    """Read-only corpus source backed by JSONL.gz files on the Hugging Face Hub.
350	
351	    For datasets whose ``load_dataset`` loading script is deprecated (e.g.
352	    ``miracl/miracl-corpus``), individual shard files are accessed directly via
353	    :class:`huggingface_hub.HfFileSystem` rather than the ``datasets`` library.
354	    The caller supplies a glob pattern relative to the repo root; matching shards
355	    are read in alphabetical order so the result is deterministic.
356	
357	    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — MIRACL corpus
358	        as the fidelity substrate for eval; every docid in the qrels must land in
359	        the built index. Local copy: ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.
360	
361	    Assumptions:
362	        - All files matched by ``path_pattern`` are JSONL compressed with gzip
363	          (``.jsonl.gz``). Mixed or uncompressed shards are not supported.
364	        - ``filter_column`` + ``filter_values`` are designed for docid-set filters
365	          (thousands of values, O(1) set lookup per row). Pass the full qrel docid
366	          set to guarantee the fidelity rule: every qrels-positive doc is in the
367	          raw snapshot, so recall is never artificially capped. When both are
368	          ``None`` the whole dataset streams through; ``max_rows`` caps it.
369	        - Row counting across shards follows shard alphabetical order. A partial
370	          last shard is consumed only to the cap — its remaining bytes are not
371	          downloaded.
372	
373	    Alternatives rejected:
374	        - Extending :class:`HuggingFaceDataset` with a ``file_mode`` flag: the
375	          two loading paths (``load_dataset`` vs ``HfFileSystem + gzip``) import
376	          entirely different libraries and share zero logic. A flag would produce
377	          a class with two unrelated personalities. A dedicated class keeps each
378	          path independently followable.
379	        - ``hf_hub_download`` per shard (requires enumerating all shard names
380	          up front): ``HfFileSystem.glob`` lists the directory lazily without
381	          materialising every path, which is what streaming decompression needs.
382	
383	    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``).
384	    """
385	
386	    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
387	    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"
388	
389	    def __init__(
390	        self,
391	        repo_id: str,
392	        revision: str,
393	        path_pattern: str,
394	        max_rows: int | None = None,
395	        filter_column: str | None = None,
396	        filter_values: list[str] | None = None,
397	        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
398	    ) -> None:
399	        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
400	        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
401	            msg = (
402	                f"HfFileDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
403	                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
404	                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
405	                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
406	            )
407	            raise DatasetError(msg)
408	        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
409	            msg = (
410	                f"HfFileDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
411	                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}."
412	            )
413	            raise DatasetError(msg)
414	        self._repo_id = repo_id
415	        self._revision = revision
416	        self._path_pattern = path_pattern
417	        self._max_rows = max_rows
418	        self._filter_column = filter_column
419	        # Convert to a set once so per-row lookup is O(1).
420	        self._filter_values: frozenset[str] | None = (
421	            frozenset(filter_values) if filter_values is not None else None
422	        )
423	        self._token_env = token_env
424	
425	    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
426	        import gzip
427	        import json
428	
429	        try:
430	            from huggingface_hub import HfFileSystem
431	        except ImportError as exc:
432	            msg = (
433	                "HfFileDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
434	                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
435	            )
436	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
437	
438	        token = os.environ.get(self._token_env) or None
439	        fs = HfFileSystem(token=token)
440	
441	        # HfFileSystem uses path format  datasets/{repo_id}@{revision}/{path}
442	        hf_glob = f"datasets/{self._repo_id}@{self._revision}/{self._path_pattern}"
443	        try:
444	            shard_paths = sorted(fs.glob(hf_glob))
445	        except Exception as exc:
446	            msg = (
447	                f"HfFileDataset({self._repo_id!r}): failed to list shards "
448	                f"matching {self._path_pattern!r} at revision {self._revision!r}: {exc}"
449	            )
450	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
451	
452	        if not shard_paths:
453	            msg = (
454	                f"HfFileDataset({self._repo_id!r}): no files matched "
455	                f"{self._path_pattern!r} at revision {self._revision!r}"
456	            )
457	            raise DatasetError(msg)
458	
459	        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
460	        filter_col = self._filter_column
461	        filter_vals = self._filter_values  # frozenset or None
462	
463	        for shard_path in shard_paths:
464	            if self._max_rows is not None and len(rows) >= self._max_rows:
465	                break
466	            try:
467	                with fs.open(shard_path, "rb") as raw_fh:
468	                    with gzip.open(raw_fh, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as gz:
469	                        for line in gz:
470	                            line = line.strip()
471	                            if not line:
472	                                continue
473	                            row = json.loads(line)
474	                            if filter_col is not None and filter_vals is not None:
475	                                if row.get(filter_col) not in filter_vals:
476	                                    continue
477	                            rows.append(row)
478	                            if self._max_rows is not None and len(rows) >= self._max_rows:
479	                                break
480	            except DatasetError:
481	                raise
482	            except Exception as exc:
483	                msg = (
484	                    f"HfFileDataset({self._repo_id!r}): error reading "
485	                    f"{shard_path!r}: {exc}"
486	                )
487	                raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
488	
489	        return rows
490	
491	    def save(self, data: None) -> None:
492	        msg = (
493	            f"HfFileDataset({self._repo_id!r}) is read-only; write the "
494	            f"normalised corpus to a JsonlDataset in data/01_raw instead."
495	        )
496	        raise DatasetError(msg)
497	
498	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
499	        return False
500	
501	    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
502	        return {
503	            "repo_id": self._repo_id,
504	            "revision": self._revision,
505	            "path_pattern": self._path_pattern,
506	            "max_rows": self._max_rows,
507	            "filter_column": self._filter_column,
508	            "filter_values_count": (
509	                len(self._filter_values) if self._filter_values is not None else None
510	            ),
511	        }
512

514	class ShardIndexDataset(AbstractDataset[dict[str, Any], Any]):
515	    """The built shard index directory, as a single catalog-addressable artifact.
516	
517	    ``save`` accepts the plain-dict payload emitted by the ``build_index`` node and
518	    performs the canonical write; ``load`` returns a query-ready
519	    :class:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex`. Keeping the conversion here means
520	    nodes stay pure functions over plain data and never touch the filesystem.
521	    """
522	
523	    def __init__(self, filepath: str) -> None:
524	        self._filepath = Path(filepath)
525	
526	    def load(self) -> Any:
527	        from cybernaut_mini.indexing import LoadedIndex
528	
529	        return LoadedIndex.load(self._filepath)
530	
531	    def save(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
532	        from cybernaut_mini.indexing import write_index
533	        from cybernaut_mini.models import Document, IndexMeta, ShardManifest
534	
535	        try:
536	            meta = IndexMeta.model_validate(data["meta"])
537	            documents = [Document.model_validate(d) for d in data["documents"]]
538	            manifests = [ShardManifest.model_validate(m) for m in data["manifests"]]
539	            vectors = np.array(data["vectors"], dtype=np.float32)
540	            doc_tokens: dict[str, list[str]] = data["doc_tokens"]
541	        except KeyError as exc:
542	            msg = f"ShardIndexDataset payload is missing key {exc}"
543	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
544	
545	        write_index(
546	            self._filepath,
547	            meta=meta,
548	            documents=documents,
549	            vectors=vectors,
550	            manifests=manifests,
551	            doc_tokens=doc_tokens,
552	        )
553	
554	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
555	        # `_VALID` is written last, so its presence is the completeness signal.
556	        return (self._filepath / "_VALID").exists()
557	
558	    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
559	        return {"filepath": str(self._filepath)}
